levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
Scenario Name: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
Description: This exercise focuses on investigating a BRICKSTORM backdoor infection in a Linux environment. The goal is to identify indicators of compromise, detect malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Access Level
levels.cloud_content:
Access the sandboxed environment using the provided Ansible playbook.
Host: c2-server
Username: cyrano
Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Connect to the target host (192.168.50.5) and next-target host (192.168.50.6) using SSH with the provided credentials.

levels.title: Identify suspicious service running on the target host
levels.solution: Use the `ps aux` command to list all processes. Search for the malware's hash (57bd98dbb5a00e54f07ffacda1fea91451a0c0b532cd7d570e98ce2ff741c21d) in the executable file name. The process name should be returned.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: The malware's hash is embedded within the executable file name.

levels.title: Detect lateral movement between hosts
levels.solution:
Use the `netstat -tuln` command to check open connections between the target (192.168.50.5) and next-target (192.168.50.6) hosts.
Look for any unusual traffic patterns or signs of file transfers using tools like `rsync`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: The malware may use a custom service or protocol for communication.

levels.title: Contain C2 communication
levels.solution: Use `iptables` to create a rule that denies incoming traffic from the C2 IP address ([redacted]) on the specified port ([redacted]).

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: The C2 IP address and port are provided in the MISP event.
